metadata.title: Ladd McConkey - Dealing with foot injury
metadata.description: McConkey was limited at Wednesday's practice due to a foot injury.
metadata.analysis: McConkey previously dealt with a rib issue this season, but he's been able to suit up for all three contests en route to a 12-183-1 line on 15 targets. He'll have two more chances this week to get back to full participation, and Friday's practice report ultimately will unveil whether or not he enters the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game at Seattle.

metadata.title: Ladd McConkey Limited With Foot Injury on Wednesday
metadata.description: Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver Ladd McConkey (foot) was listed as a limited practice participant on Wednesday. McConkey suffered a rib injury in the season-opening loss to the Arizona Cardinals and was questionable for Week 2 before ultimately suiting up. The 24-year-old is now on the injury report with a foot injury as the Bolts prepare to face the Seattle Seahawks on the road in Week 4. Through the first three games of the 2026 season, the former second-rounder from Georgia has 12 receptions for 183 yards and a touchdown on 15 targets. McConkey remains a key piece of the Chargers' passing attack, but the offense has yet to hit its stride under new coordinator Mike McDaniel through a tough early portion of their schedule. It will not get any easier for McConkey and the Chargers this weekend against Seattle's strong defense, but as long as he is cleared to play on Sunday, he should be kept in most starting fantasy lineups as one of quarterback Justin Herbert's favorite targets.

metadata.title: Ladd McConkey - Four catches in Week 3 loss
metadata.description: McConkey secured four of five targets for 66 yards in the Chargers' 24-16 loss to the Bills on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Justin Herbert's top target turned in a solid stat line in the Chargers' third straight loss to open the season, but it still wasn't enough to net Los Angeles its first win. McConkey finished second in receptions and receiving yards while slotting in third in targets on the afternoon for the Bolts, but through three contests, he sports a modest 12-183-1 line on 15 targets. It doesn't get any easier for the Chargers in Week 4, as they pay a visit to the defending champion Seahawks next Sunday afternoon.

metadata.title: Ladd McConkey hauls in four passes in Week 3 loss to Bills
metadata.description: Ladd McConkey hauled in four of his five targets for 66 yards in the Chargers' 24-16 Week 3 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
metadata.analysis: McConkey has made the most of inconsistent involvement in the Los Angeles passing attack to begin the season, posting over 65 receiving yards in two of the first three contests. The wideout remains one of the more dynamic options in an underperforming Chargers offense early on, with a tough Week 4 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks up next.

metadata.title: Ladd McConkey Off the Injury Report Heading into Week 3 vs. Bills
metadata.description: Los Angeles Chargers wideout Ladd McConkey was a full participant in every practice and is off the injury report heading into his Week 3 matchup against the Buffalo Bills. McConkey has been the centerpiece of the offense so far this season. When he is on the field, the Chargers offense has the seventh-best EPA (0.12), but when he's off the field, they have the second-worst EPA (-0.41), per JJ Zachariason of Late Round Fantasy Football. McConkey enters Week 3 as RotoBaller's PPR WR25 in an intriguing matchup. The Bills defense has allowed the 3rd-most 20-plus-yard passes (9) and the 5th-most passing yards. In addition, the Bills defense ranks near the bottom of the league in EPA and has given up too many highly valuable plays. McConkey should be viewed as a WR2 with upside as he travels across the country in Week 3.

metadata.title: Ladd McConkey (rib) logs full practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Ladd McConkey (rib) logged a full practice session to start the week on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: McConkey was able to play through his rib injury last week and is now a full participant to start this week, meaning that he is close to full health and should be fully good to go for Week 3. He had an underwhelming performance last week but has a chance to bounce back this week in what should be a competitive matchup against the Bills on Sunday.

metadata.title: Ladd McConkey Practicing in Full
metadata.description: Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver Ladd McConkey (rib) was a full participant in the team's practice on Wednesday, according to the team. McConkey took a hard hit in the Week 1 loss to the Arizona Cardinals and was questionable to play in Week 2 against the division-rival Las Vegas Raiders. The 24-year-old eventually ended up suiting up in a second straight loss for the Bolts and caught all three of his targets for a pedestrian 35 receiving yards. The former second-rounder from Georgia looked much better before his injury in Week 1, catching five of seven targets for 82 yards and his first touchdown of the 2026 season. McConkey looks to have moved past his rib injury as the Chargers prepare for a difficult battle on the road against the Buffalo Bills this Sunday. Barring a setback, he should be active in Week 3 and should be considered a strong WR2 in PPR formats as the Chargers look to finally get their offense clicking.

metadata.title: Ladd McConkey underwhelming in loss Sunday
metadata.description: Ladd McConkey caught three passes for 35 yards in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.
metadata.analysis: McConkey was able to play on Sunday, despite being questionable coming into the week due to an injury he suffered in Week 1. He didn't look very good against the Raiders, however, totaling just 35 yards over the course of the afternoon. He will likely bounce back and return to being a good fantasy option in the near future, but his consistency may be frustrating if Los Angeles' offense continues to struggle.

metadata.title: Ladd McConkey - Three grabs in Week 2 loss
metadata.description: McConkey (ribs) secured all three targets for 35 yards in the Chargers' 26-14 loss to the Raiders on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: McConkey gained clearance from his questionable tag due to a rib injury to suit up, and the third-year wideout tied for the team lead in receptions while finishing second in receiving yards. However, it was a lackluster and mistake-filled day overall for the Chargers passing attack, so McConkey's numbers should also be viewed in that context. McConkey should play a critical role as Los Angeles looks to avoid what would be an alarming third straight loss to open the season in a Week 3 road showdown against the Bills next Sunday.

metadata.title: Ladd McConkey Guts Out Three Catches in Week 2 Loss
metadata.description: Los Angeles Chargers wideout Ladd McConkey (ribs) caught all three of his targets for 35 yards in Sunday's devastating 26-14 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders. The 24-year-old was questionable heading into the matchup with a rib injury he sustained after a hard hit in Week 1. McConkey wore a flak jacket under his uniform for extra protection. However, McConkey still took a dip in targets, likely due to his injury after being the focal point of the offense in the season opener. Through two games, he has caught eight of his 10 targets for 117 yards and one touchdown. Unfortunately, McConkey will be battling this rib injury for an extended period of time and will cap his fantasy ceiling moving forward. McConkey and the Chargers will head on the road for the first time this season to face the Buffalo Bills in Week 3.

metadata.title: Ladd McConkey (ribs) officially active for Week 2
metadata.description: Chargers WR Ladd McConkey (ribs) is officially active for a Week 2 matchup with the Raiders.
metadata.analysis: McConkey is dealing with a cracked rib but was pushing to play through the injury. With McConkey active, fantasy managers should expect him to operate as the top wide receiver for the Chargers in a divisional matchup with the Raiders.

metadata.title: Ladd McConkey - Active for Week 2
metadata.description: McConkey (ribs) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Raiders, Kris Rhim of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Separate reports leading up to the game indicated that McConkey intended to play, and he will indeed suit up for Week 2. McConkey is apparently playing through a cracked rib and will sport a flak jacket, so while he will be out there, it's unclear if he will fill his usual role.

metadata.title: Ladd McConkey - Trending toward playing Week 2
metadata.description: McConkey (ribs), who is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Raiders, is "trending in the right direction" ahead of the 4:05 p.m. ET kickoff, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
metadata.analysis: Official word on McConkey's status will arrive when the Chargers post their inactive list 90 minutes prior to kickoff, but unless he experiences a setback with his cracked rib while warming up Sunday, the third-year wideout is on track to suit up. Schefter relayed earlier Sunday that McConkey will wear a flak jacket to protect his injured rib if he does wind up playing.

metadata.title: Ladd McConkey Active Against Raiders
metadata.description: Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver Ladd McConkey (rib) is officially active for Sunday's game against the Las Vegas Raiders, according to Alex Insdorf. McConkey missed practice Wednesday and Thursday before getting back on the field in a limited capacity Friday, and he carried a questionable tag into Sunday. He caught five passes for 82 yards and a touchdown in the season opener against Arizona. McConkey will give it a go against Las Vegas despite the rib injury, keeping one of Justin Herbert's primary options in the lineup. Fantasy managers who were considering using Quentin Johnston or Tre'Harris in a flex spot this weekend due to McConkey's injury might want to go in another direction now.

metadata.title: Ladd McConkey (ribs) pushing to play Sunday
metadata.description: Ladd McConkey (ribs) is pushing to play on Sunday against the Raiders despite a cracked rib. There is optimism that he will play, as the team did not elevate a wide receiver from the practice squad this week. If he plays, he will be wearing a flak jacket.
metadata.analysis: If Ladd goes, it's hard to imagine sitting him given how important he is to this offense. Tre Harris and Quentin Johnston could get some additional work, but Ladd will be the main man in town if active.
